scope: Primary evidence for temporal melt-pool structure, frame registration, frame-deletion localization, and the limits of transferring a same-video synthetic test to a naturally incomplete record.

confirmedFacts.claim: NIST treats each co-axial melt-pool frame as a time-specific observation and constructs spatiotemporal features only after associating frames with process position; temporal structure is informative but does not itself supply an exposure identity ledger.
NIST's generalized superposition work preserves temporal information alongside registered melt-pool features because individual frames and their neighborhood carry different physical information.

NIST camera-registration work requires calibrated command, measurement, trigger, and shutter delays; image continuity cannot replace those calibrations when the claim is absolute process-coordinate identity.
confirmedFacts.resultPeriod: AMMT and commercial-system registration case studies

confirmedFacts.claim: Frame-deletion forensics has used temporal discontinuities and compression-domain periodicity to localize edit breakpoints, but its assumptions concern encoded consumer video and cannot be imported unchanged into a lossless scientific camera stream.
Bidirectional flow and temporal interpolation are established ways to test whether two endpoints admit a plausible intermediate frame, while occlusion and nonlinear motion remain known failure modes.
The public X16 record supplies lossless Lagarith AVI products and command/measurement archives but no public camera tick ledger or trigger-to-frame sidecar identified in its manifest.

inferences: A same-layer synthetic deletion can test whether the exported image sequence contains enough cadence information to expose a missing interval without assuming cross-layer frame correspondence.

The relevant contrast is not simply a large adjacent-frame difference: a deletion seam should resemble an intact pair separated by two to nine acquisition steps more than it resembles a one-step pair in the same local state.
Passing a synthetic test would establish a detector's bounded error on injected omissions in L0002, not the location or cause of L0001's natural 23-frame deficit.
unverifiedProposals: A self-supervised gap discriminator trained only on intact L0002 cadence can separate one-step transitions from two-to-nine-step transitions at useful whole-partition false-discovery control.

Multiscale intensity, tail geometry, and local motion ratios can outperform RC44's 8 by 8 command-to-image prediction because they test the deletion seam directly rather than predicting image content from commands.
If the detector passes a sealed L0002 development gate, independently selected layers can measure transport error before any natural L0001 call is permitted.

searchStrategy.priority: NIST data and primary NIST papers first, then original peer-reviewed video-forensics and frame-interpolation papers. Blogs, tutorials, and vendor marketing are excluded.
searchStrategy.noveltyBoundary: RC47 does not claim that deletion forensics, multiscale temporal differences, LDA, or self-supervised gap classification is new. The proposed contribution is their preregistered use as a scientific-instrument cadence test with a sealed natural record, explicit refusal, and a later cross-layer transport gate.
